About the Role
As BlueCore's first dedicated Finance Lead, you will build the company's financial backbone from scratch and report directly to the CEO. You will own the books end to end, including every capital purchase for the warehouse and the barge, making sure it is tracked, reconciled, and always audit-ready. You will work closely with the CEO on financial planning, reporting, fundraising, and board materials, and with Supply Chain and Manufacturing to understand where the company's capital is actually going as we build out Long Beach. You will have massive ownership over how the finance function is shaped here, while collaborating with our greater leadership team. 
Responsibilities 
Own the full accounting cycle, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, general ledger, and monthly close, ensuring every transaction is accurately recorded and reconciled.
Build the company's core financial infrastructure from the ground up: chart of accounts, internal controls, approval workflows, and close processes that scale as the company grows.
Develop and maintain financial models, budgets, and forecasts, including burn rate, runway, and cash flow visibility for the CEO and the board.
Keep the company diligence-ready at all times: a clean data room, well-organized financials, and clear documentation so BlueCore can move quickly whenever leadership needs it.
Partner directly with the CEO on financial reporting and board materials, translating company performance into a clear, accurate narrative.
Track capital and project expenditures tied to the Long Beach factory buildout and barge construction, working with Supply Chain and Manufacturing to understand cost drivers and maintain accurate cost accounting.
Select and implement the accounting systems and tools the company needs to scale finance operations, from accounting software to expense management to ERP integration.
Ensure compliance with GAAP and applicable tax and regulatory filings, and build the financial recordkeeping practices that will support a future audit.
Manage vendor and contractor payments and cash management, and build cost-control mechanisms appropriate for a capital-intensive startup.
Required Qualifications & Skills
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.
5+ years of progressive experience in accounting or finance, with direct ownership of a company's books, close process, and financial reporting.
Demonstrated experience building financial systems, controls, and processes from the ground up at an early-stage or high-growth startup.
Strong working knowledge of GAAP, financial statements, and the full accounting cycle.
Experience preparing financial diligence packages, data rooms, and investor-facing reporting.
A meticulous, ownership-driven approach to the numbers: you catch what others miss and treat every dollar as if it were your own.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to work directly and candidly with the CEO and executive leadership.
Desired Qualifications & Skills
CPA license or MBA.
Prior finance experience in a capital-intensive, highly regulated industry (nuclear, aerospace, defense, or similar).
Experience selecting and implementing an ERP or accounting system as a company scales.
Familiarity with cost accounting for physical products, including component/BOM costing and CAPEX tracking.
Experience working in a venture- or private equity-backed company through a period of high growth.

Responsibilities 

  • Provide comprehensive neutronics support, establishing core geometry, enrichment, lattice, beryllium reflector, and rotating-drum control architecture.

  • Own criticality, reactivity coefficients (MTC, Doppler), kinetics, depletion, and cycle length.

Principal Thermal-Hydraulics & Safety Analysis Engineer

About the Role

The Principal Thermal-Hydraulics & Safety Analysis Engineer operates at the critical intersection of fluids, structural mechanics, and safety. You will convert the reactor heat source into a safe, sized coolant system by wearing multiple hats. In this role, you will model system thermal-hydraulics, perform mechanical sizing for the primary, secondary, and tertiary loops, and author the Chapter 15 safety analyses for our Preliminary and Final Safety Analysis Reports (PSAR/FSAR). 

Responsibilities 

  • Own system thermal-hydraulics modeling (nodalization, LOCA, natural circulation) and subchannel Departure from Nucleate Boiling Ratio (DNBR) and hot-channel analysis.

  • Perform mechanical sizing for the reactor pressure vessel, steam generator, pressurizer, and reactor coolant pumps.

  • Establish primary, secondary, and tertiary heat balances and flows, including seawater heat rejection support.

  • Author the Chapter 15 transient and accident thermal-hydraulic evaluations and coordinate them with the broader risk-informed safety case. 

  • Set the minimum-DNBR using 95/95 Specified Acceptable Fuel Design Limits (SAFDL) and validate the CHF correlation basis. 

  • Manage fatigue and fracture margins in mechanical component design.

  • Manage coupled neutronics and thermal-hydraulics feedback in close coordination with the Core Physics team.

Required Qualifications & Skills

  • MS or PhD in Nuclear or Mechanical Engineering with a specialization in reactor thermal-hydraulics or pressure-vessel design. 

  • Demonstrated hands-on experience running system thermal-hydraulics codes (e.g., RELAP5-3D, TRACE, or ATHLET).

  • Experience running subchannel codes (e.g., VIPRE-01, COBRA-TF/CTF) for MDNBR and hot-channel factor evaluation. 

  • Deep understanding of ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code, Section III, Division 1, Subsection NB (Class 1) for primary component design-by-analysis.

  • Ability to size a steam generator and heat exchangers from heat balances using formulas.

  • Experience sizing reactor pressure vessel walls utilizing membrane hoop thickness formulas. 

Desired Qualifications & Skills

  • Experience designing primary, secondary, and tertiary loop components for marine or compact-PWR environments. 

  • Familiarity with ANSYS or ABAQUS structural FEA to evaluate components under dynamic marine loads.

  • Deep understanding of 10 CFR 50 Appendix G fracture-toughness requirements and embrittlement shifts over vessel life.

  • Familiarity with applying shock and wave dynamic loading constraints to primary component mounts and structures.

  • Experience integrating deterministic Chapter 15 safety results with a broader Probabilistic Risk Assessment (PRA).

By designing and building advanced floating Pressurized Water Reactors (PWRs) on barges right here in Long Beach, CA, we are bringing scalable, clean, and reliable power to the world. Joining our team means getting in on the ground floor of a revolution in marine small modular reactors (SMRs). If you are passionate, driven, and ready to tackle some of the most exciting challenges of our time, we want you on our team!

Our Values

  • Humility — We hold strong opinions loosely, say "I don't know," ask for help early, and let the best idea win regardless of who it came from.

  • Inclusivity — The best engineering comes from many perspectives. We build a team where everyone is heard, and we mean it.

  • Pragmatism — We solve the real problem in front of us, reuse what already works, and value a tested answer over an elegant one.


About the Role

As one of our first engineers, you'll work across power, instrumentation, and control systems to make our reactor real. From instrumentation, to the power generation, distribution, and storage systems, and networking and computing, you'll work hands-on with all of it in a fast-paced environment. You'll decide what to buy and what to build to lower cost, improve reliability and performance, and shorten production and deployment timelines.

Responsibilities 

  • Own electrical systems from concept through commissioning.

  • Perform design trades, develop requirements, and bring up and validate hardware.

  • Develop schematics, wiring diagrams, and data acquisition systems.

  • Collaborate with the Mechanical, Software, Core Design, and Quality teams to design the reactor.

  • Work with the Licensing team regarding the design basis, including fail-safe architecture, design diversity, and redundancy.

  • Support the hazard analysis process by identifying failure modes, safe states, and mitigations.

  • Support test activities including HITL, validation testing, and integration campaigns.

  • Develop new hardware and processes to improve safety and reliability, enhance existing capabilities, bring new capabilities online, reduce cost, and shrink manufacturing time.

Required Qualifications & Skills

  • A degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or a related discipline.

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience activating, building, and troubleshooting complex electronic systems.

  • Familiar with fault-tolerant, safety-critical, and/or autonomous systems.

  • Hands-on experience with multiple electrical domains: instrumentation, sensing, power systems, controls, networking, computing, data acquisition, etc.

  • Proficient with lab instrumentation (oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, signal generators).

  • Able to think through possible failure modes and safe states.

  • Comfortable reasoning from first principles.

  • Works independently and drives tasks to completion with minimal direction.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Desired Qualifications & Skills

  • Experience with kV level voltage and MW level power systems.

  • Experience designing to nuclear, maritime, or other safety-critical standards.

  • Proficiency with electrical design, simulation, and/or PCB layout tools.

About the Role
As the Supply Chain Lead at BlueCore Energy, you will build and manage the procurement and supplier network required to bring our advanced floating Pressurized Water Reactor (PWR) to life. Operating at the critical intersection of nuclear engineering and maritime construction, you will bridge the gap between engineering design and our supplier base, ensuring that components for both primary and secondary loops meet rigorous nuclear standards. In this foundational role, you will stand up procurement engineering, commercial-grade dedication, and counterfeit-parts controls while working closely with finance and quality teams to establish the entire nuclear-qualified supply chain and shipyard qualification plan.
 
Responsibilities 
Capture and translate complex engineering requirements into actionable supplier specifications for primary and secondary loop components.  
Identify, vet, and onboard suppliers capable of delivering high-quality, nuclear-grade materials and components.  
Select, implement, and manage an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system to handle inventory control, ordering, and logistics.  
Negotiate contracts, manage procurement costs, and establish robust cost-control mechanisms for the startup phase and beyond.  
Work closely with the Quality team to ensure all suppliers comply with relevant quality standards (ASME NQA-1 and 10 CFR 50 Appendix B).  
Stand up the supplier audit and corrective action program (CAP) processes across our vendor network.  
Build out a nuclear-qualified supply chain alongside a comprehensive shipyard qualification plan.  
Own procurement engineering, commercial-grade dedication (CGD), and counterfeit-parts controls across all procurement streams.  
Partner with finance and leadership on make-vs-buy analyses and the capital planning of long-lead procurement items.  
Establish document control, records management, and configuration management systems to ensure full component traceability and pedigree.
Required Qualifications & Skills
Proven experience in supply chain management within nuclear, aerospace, marine, or highly regulated heavy manufacturing industries.  
Demonstrated experience successfully implementing and scaling Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems in a manufacturing environment.  
Solid understanding of procurement engineering principles, contract negotiation, and inventory logistics.  
Practical familiarity with 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality assurance criteria and vendor management practices.  
Experience establishing vendor audit controls, receipt inspections, and component traceability processes.  
Strong track record of technical collaboration with engineering, quality, and finance teams.
Desired Qualifications & Skills
Strong familiarity with ASME NQA-1 standards and nuclear supply chain requirements is highly preferred.  
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Quality, or a related technical discipline.  
Direct experience leading or supporting an ASME NQA-1 program and establishing nuclear-qualified vendor networks.  
Hands-on experience with commercial-grade dedication (CGD) per EPRI guidelines and 10 CFR Part 21 defect reporting rules.  
Familiarity with shipyard and commercial marine quality assurance interfaces, weld qualifications, and non-destructive examination (NDE) standards.  
Proven capability in designing counterfeit and fraudulent parts prevention controls.
